claim: Fix \(m=15/16\) in the Kominers blunted quarter-disk support-function family and restrict to \(0\le\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_*\), where \(\varepsilon_*=(1/2-k)/(1-q\cos m)=0.70808413910758175\ldots\). Then every body on this slice is reduced of thickness \(1\), including the endpoint where one curvature radius vanishes only at the active-arc endpoints; the area is strictly increasing in \(\varepsilon\), so the endpoint is the unique slice maximizer, with area \(0.78718352669640537\ldots\), strictly above both \(\pi/4\) and the published \(\varepsilon=13/20\) example.
scientific_integrity: The all-parameter monotonicity on the stated slice is proved from an exact quadratic area formula. Endpoint convexity and reducedness are checked separately. Transcendental inequalities used in the numerical constants are enclosed by exact rational alternating-series bounds in verify.py.
scientific_limitations: The result optimizes only the nonnegative epsilon slice with m fixed to 15/16. It does not optimize over m, over the full two-parameter family, or over all reduced planar bodies.
title: Exact area optimizer on the fixed-angle blunted quarter-disk slice
